ypbind.why: NIS client binding daemon; a real, named Unix service program with a man page.

nscd.why: Name Service Cache Daemon; a real, widely documented system daemon. Memory leak suits systems people.

sendmail.why: Mail transfer daemon; one of the best-known Unix daemons, so off-by-one fits.

ypserv.why: NIS server daemon; a real named service. Systems-specialist tier is plausible.

dovecot.why: IMAP/POP3 server daemon; a real, widely deployed service. Null pointer exception fits many sysadmins.

nginx.why: Web server daemon; very common, so off-by-one is right.

rpc.ypxfrd.why: NIS map transfer daemon, named as rpc.ypxfrd in its man page. Niche, but a real service and only NIS-literate people know it, so the heisenbug tier is acceptable.

rwhod.why: rwho status daemon from BSD; a real, named legacy service. Race condition suits specialists.

bsnmpd.why: FreeBSD SNMP daemon, named in its man page. Deep-internals tier fits.

dockerd.why: Docker engine daemon; a real, widely known service. Null pointer exception fits many people.

nfscbd.why: FreeBSD NFSv4 callback daemon, named in its man page. Deep-internals tier fits.

comsat.why: BSD mail-notification daemon (biff's backend), named in its man page and a real service. Membership holds, but it's a legacy name, not a deep-internals one, so heisenbug is too deep. Race or leak fits better.

dhcpd.why: DHCP server daemon; a real, widely known service. Null pointer exception fits.

tcpd.why: TCP wrapper: inetd runs it per connection as an access-control shim that then execs the service. It is not a background service in its own right.

mysqld.why: MySQL server daemon; a real, widely known service. Null pointer exception fits.

cupsd.why: CUPS print scheduler daemon; a real named service. Null pointer exception fits.

rtadvd.why: IPv6 router advertisement daemon, named in its man page. Race condition suits specialists.

xinetd.why: Extended inetd super-server daemon; a real, named service. Null pointer exception fits.

postgres.why: PostgreSQL server process, the postgres daemon; a real named service. Null pointer exception fits.

sshd.why: SSH server daemon; one of the best-known Unix daemons, so off-by-one is right.
